criteria.reason: The fixture /refine-design run read the recorded canvas and got 404 Not Found, republished the canvas from the committed docs/ui/demo/canvas/ files (new artifact 8kQAqisabu8R5LtmcXLaFJ), carried on with the heading edit and ended COMMAND COMPLETE, not STUCK. refine-design-map.json holds the new canvas URL.

No no-access fixture exists. The Artifact tool returns one combined error for a deleted artifact and for one not shared with this account, and no artifact owned by another account is available in the authorized environments. A genuine no-access read was never exercised.

The fixture /design-system --sync run read the recorded system page and got 404 Not Found, rebuilt and published a new Design System page (AoipErp9HpZ7u7so8gz9Mv) from docs/ui/_design-system/acme/, recorded it in design-map.json and ended COMMAND COMPLETE. Shown for not-found; the no-access path cannot be produced here (FS-2).

After the canvas republish, the canvases entry holds the new URL 8kQAqisabu8R5LtmcXLaFJ with previous_url equal to the replaced ...00000000c0de; dsys-design-map.json shows the same for the /design-system run.

artifacts.json design entry holds the new canvas url with previous_url ...c0de, and the design-system entry holds the new system url with previous_url ...0d5; dsys-artifacts-shared.json shows the same for the /design-system run.
design_system block after /design-system --sync holds the new url AoipErp9HpZ7u7so8gz9Mv and previous_url ...0000000000d5, the URL that failed to read.

artifacts.js record with OLD then NEW url, then get/read: the entry holds url NEW-URL and previous_url OLD-URL, and a third record with the same url keeps previous_url. The library sets previous_url itself on a URL change rather than via a flag, which keeps the field as required.

The /refine-design readouts state the canvas and system republish in DECISIONS, naming old and new URLs. The /design-system --sync readout (transcript-design-system-sync-unreadable.txt) does not: the replacement of the unreadable system page and canvas is reported only in STATE, and its DECISIONS section never mentions it, contrary to the contract line the command points to. The build was reached and did the wrong thing for /design-system.

design-mirror.js check against the new canvas URL and its recorded version returns "unchanged", and against the replaced URL reports no matching canvas; refine-design-map.json shows the new canvas with a fresh version and synced_at. The sync base belongs to the new canvas.

Partial evidence only. The transcript shows the canvas read failing with 'not an artifact URL' and the run then editing the board heading with no Artifact publish or create call, which is the right behaviour so far, and the after-snapshots still hold the original URLs with no previous_url. But the capture stops while the visual critic is still running, before the command's commit-and-record step, which is where a publish would happen. The criterion's evidence calls for design-map.json and artifacts.json after the run, and the run had not finished (tmux session fs10 still waiting on the critic at 02:04). Nothing seen shows the build misbehaving, but the end state is unproven.

Report A labels the two reused misses as coming from Acme.Card (lib.js) with no accept-or-fix call recorded, while the hand-drawn caption, button and disabled control carry no reused label (the caption is located in 01-home.dc.html); the measured values mark the reused ones "(reused)". Every contrast and target-size miss is placed in one of the two classes.

With a brief.md ruling recorded (report B), the hand-drawn caption contrast 1.92:1 and the Drawn tiny and Disabled ctl target-size misses are ranked [high]; they are also high in report A (no ruling) and report C (design.md ruling).
With the ruling in brief.md Accessibility caveats, the reused "library low contrast" and "lib tiny" misses appear as "[low] (known build-side caveat, reused component)", not as high findings.
With the ruling only in design.md section 4 (brief.md caveats None), report C lists the reused contrast and target-size misses as low, "KNOWN build-side caveat (reused component)".
With no ruling in brief.md or design.md, report A ranks the reused contrast and target-size misses [high] with a hint to record a call, and no build-side-caveat label.
sha256 of .claude/rules/design.md is identical before and after the variant C /audit-design run, and git diff --stat on it is empty.

The fixture board holds a disabled button and an aria-disabled div, both #bbbbbb (1.92:1). The measures list them only as target-size misses (count 2, 120x20) and give no contrast entry for either; report A has no contrast finding for them. The screenshot shows both controls in light grey.

The non-reused contrast entry has count 2: the caption plus the "Why disabled: sign in first" text, the only other non-disabled #bbbbbb element on the board, so the explanatory text is still measured. The disabled controls carry target-size misses at 120x20, and report A lists Disabled ctl as [high] below 44px.

/refine-design --auto with no feedback after the brief-ruling audit fixed the ordinary findings (caption contrast, 44px buttons, overflow, copy, title) and left the x-import Acme.Card untouched; the readout lists the two library-card caveats as accepted in the brief, not acted on. The after screenshot shows the card unchanged and the rest redrawn.
